name: Shavemaxxing

card.summary: Optimising face shaving and grooming so the skin looks smooth, the jawline is clearly defined and facial hair looks deliberate.
card.note: Irritation, razor bumps and ingrown hairs are the usual downsides.

quick.overview:
Shavemaxxing is the practice of treating shaving as an appearance upgrade: a clean, even shave shows the jaw, chin and skin, removes stubble shadow and makes a face look groomed. It is a basic grooming step in style-focused looksmaxxing.

Research on facial hair reports that clean-shaven faces are rated less dominant than bearded ones, so the choice between shaving and beard is part of how a face reads. Skin effects of shaving, such as razor burn and bumps, are described in dermatology and general references.
quick.how: People choose a razor type (safety or cartridge razor, straight razor, or electric shaver), soften hair with warm water, use lubricant, shave in light passes and finish with a moisturising aftershave. Electric shavers cut less closely but cause fewer nicks; trimmers are used first on long hair.
quick.risks: Cuts, razor burn and razor bumps (pseudofolliculitis barbae) are the common problems. Wikipedia notes that shaving does not make hair grow back thicker or darker.

lead: Shavemaxxing refers to optimising the shave to improve facial appearance. A smooth, evenly shaved face shows the shape of the jaw and chin, and gives a groomed look that proponents treat as a low-cost improvement.

Shaving is removing hair with a razor or other bladed tool. Copper razors date to about 3000 BC, the safety razor was patented in 1876, King Camp Gillette introduced a double-edged version in 1895, and the first electric razor was built by Jacob Schick in 1928.[2]

Clean-shaven fashion has risen and fallen: Roman men were largely clean-shaven, beards returned in the sixteenth century, and clean-shaven faces dominated again in the twentieth century, helped by Gillette's advertising, before full beards came back among young men in the 2010s.[1] Perception research reported on Wikipedia finds clean-shaven faces rated as less dominant than bearded ones.[1]

chain: Smooth skin, no stubble shadow, sharp jaw and neckline
angle.text: A good shave exposes the jawline and skin and removes uneven stubble. Doing it with suitable tools and skin care also limits irritation that would undercut the result.

infobox: Safety/cartridge razor, straight razor, electric shaver, trimmer

paras: Wet shaving uses straight or safety razors with warm water and a lubricating cream, soap or gel, typically in several light passes with aftershave optional. Electric (dry) shaving uses oscillating or rotating blades behind a screen, which reduces cuts and needs no lather but may not cut as close. Trimmers shorten long hair before shaving.[2]

Wikipedia describes cuts, razor burn (often from a dull blade, dry shaving, pressure or shaving against the grain) and razor bumps, a persistent inflammation from ingrown hairs known as pseudofolliculitis barbae. Moisture, lubrication, shaving with the grain and moisturising aftershave are listed as ways people reduce irritation.[2]
Shaving does not alter hair thickness or colour; cut hair feels coarser because the tip is blunt.[2]

Reports summarised on Wikipedia indicate clean-shaven faces are seen as less dominant than bearded faces, and that facial hairiness appears to influence male attractiveness, with scholars undecided whether the effect concerns attractiveness or dominance.[1]
No studies found on shavemaxxing as a practice.

timeline.event: King Camp Gillette introduces a double-edged safety razor; commercial production begins in 1903.[2]
Jacob Schick builds the first electric razor.[2]
